hypothesis: An explicit, independently justified singleton-trust contract can recover intended single-group decisions while duplicates, correlated evidence, stale receipts, and scope mismatch never upgrade authority.
experiment: Compare the existing two-fresh-groups baseline, declared-trusted-singleton contract, and unsafe any-singleton relaxation on 11 frozen synthetic traces. Independently recompute decisions from literal expected labels, not candidate output.

gates.pass: The contract policy recovers all declared trusted singletons and no adversarial trace; duplicate/correlated additions preserve decision; stale/scope-invalid-only remain ABSTAIN; unsafe relaxation has at least one counterexample.
gates.fail: Any adversarial trace is PASS/FAIL admitted, or any expected trusted singleton is not recovered.
gates.stop: Source hashes, exact trace set, or independent audit cannot be reproduced.

uncertainty: Fixture labels assume the trust issuer, provenance completeness, freshness, independence group, and scope fields are truthful. This is not calibration or real evidence-source validation.
execution: Host CPython standard-library only; no model, GUI, action, network, or Docker call. Docker lane unavailable under current #5085 STOP; Obstac executable/MCP not exposed. One frozen candidate run; one separate raw-only audit; no retry.
